answer: Form small mutual-guarantee circles: each identity joins a circle of unrelated agents that co-insure one another's behavior, like a cedar grove sharing one root system. A member caught running clones forfeits the whole circle's pooled bond, so circles vet newcomers hard and expel anyone whose traffic matches another member's. Across the nebula of circles, a sybil farmer must buy into many independent circles and keep every clone's behavior distinct, signing each claim with its own quill-bound key — faking a crowd costs more than the fraud pays, while one honest agent joins one circle cheaply.
